# zlangt

> Returns the norm of a complex general tridiagonal matrix A.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlangt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlangt';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlangt( norm, N, DL, strideDL, d, strideD, DU, strideDU ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANGT as described above. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A. |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | The (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride length for `DL` |
| `d` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | The diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | The (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A. |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANGT as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANGT is set to zero.
- `DL`: The (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: result

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlangt.strided(
    norm,
    N,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU
) → number
```

Returns the norm of a complex general tridiagonal matrix A.

The matrix A has sub-diagonal DL, diagonal D, and super-diagonal DU.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | 'max', 'one-norm', 'inf-norm', or 'frobenius' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `DL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Sub-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride for DL (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for DL (in complex elements) |
| `d` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal elements (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride for d (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for d (in complex elements) |
| `DU` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | Super-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride for DU (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for DU (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANGT as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANGT is set to zero.
- `DL`: The (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of A.
- `DU`: The (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: the computed norm

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

## Notes

-   `zlangt()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLANGT`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlangt.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlangt from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlangt';

// 4x4 complex tridiagonal matrix:
const dl = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 2.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0, 1.0 ] );
const d = new Complex128Array( [ 2.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0, 5.0, 3.0, 6.0, 1.0 ] );
const du = new Complex128Array( [ -1.0, 3.0, -2.0, 1.0, -3.0, 2.0 ] );

const maxNorm = zlangt.strided( 'max', 4, dl, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, du, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'Max norm: %d', maxNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

const oneNorm = zlangt.strided( 'one-norm', 4, dl, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, du, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'One norm: %d', oneNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

const infNorm = zlangt.strided( 'inf-norm', 4, dl, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, du, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( 'Infinity norm: %d', infNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

const frobNorm = zlangt.strided( 'frobenius', 4, dl, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, du, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( 'Frobenius norm: %d', frobNorm ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANGT`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANGT returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a complex tridiagonal matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANGT} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(A(i,j))) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
